title: Context across HttpClient and queues
summary: HttpClient carries the trace for you; a message queue does not. Client spans, producer and consumer spans, inject and extract, links, and a local viewer for all of it.

steps.title: HTTP: automatic. Everything else: you.
body: Calls through `HttpClient` already send `traceparent` (from `Activity.Current`), and ASP.NET Core continues it on the other side.
Add `.AddHttpClientInstrumentation()` to get a **Client** span per call (`GET`, with `server.address`, `url.full`,
`http.response.status_code`): it is the edge between two services on the service map, and its duration includes the network.
A message broker, a database-backed job table or an in-memory `Channel` carries nothing by itself. The producer must **inject** the
context into the message's headers and the consumer must **extract** it:
using var send = Source.StartActivity("orders publish", ActivityKind.Producer);
// consumer (often much later, on another machine)
using var process = Source.StartActivity("orders process", ActivityKind.Consumer, parent.ActivityContext);
Name messaging spans `{operation} {destination}` (`orders publish`, `orders process`) and add `messaging.system.name`,
`messaging.destination.name` and `messaging.operation.type` (development conventions, so pin and expect renames). Broker client
libraries increasingly do this for you (RabbitMQ.Client 7 has an ActivitySource; Confluent.Kafka needs a wrapper).

steps.title: Trace the call to the tax service
prompt: `GET /quote/{amount}` calls the tax service `GET /tax/{amount}` over HTTP (here the tax endpoint lives in the same app; the starter
builds the URL from the incoming request). The trace shows only the two server spans, with nothing linking them visibly.
Add the **HttpClient instrumentation** to the tracer provider, so the call gets its own **Client** span. Check the result: the tax
service's server span must be a child of that client span, all in one trace (drawn under the results).
starter: app.MapGet("/quote/{amount:double}", async (double amount, HttpRequest req, IHttpClientFactory http) =>
return Results.Ok(new { amount, tax = tax?.tax, total = amount + (tax?.tax ?? 0) });
solution: app.MapGet("/quote/{amount:double}", async (double amount, HttpRequest req, IHttpClientFactory http) =>
return Results.Ok(new { amount, tax = tax?.tax, total = amount + (tax?.tax ?? 0) });
hints: One more call on the tracing builder.
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
var r = await http.GetAsync("/quote/50");
DojoWeb.Status("GET /quote/50 answers 200", 200, r);
Dojo.Eq("total", "60", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(r), "total"));
var quote = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.DisplayName == "GET /quote/{amount:double}");
var client = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.Kind == ActivityKind.Client && DojoOtel.Tag(a, "url.full").Contains("/tax/"));
await DojoOtel.Settle();
var tax = DojoOtel.Spans.FirstOrDefault(a => a.DisplayName == "GET /tax/{amount:double}");
Dojo.Check("a client span for the outgoing call", client is not null, "Spans: " + string.Join(", ", DojoOtel.Spans.Select(a => a.DisplayName)));
Dojo.Eq("it is named after the method", "GET", client?.DisplayName);

Dojo.Check("it has the stable HTTP client attributes", DojoOtel.Tag(client, "url.full").Contains("/tax/50") && DojoOtel.Tag(client, "http.response.status_code") == "200", "url.full=" + DojoOtel.Tag(client, "url.full"));
Dojo.Check("the client span is a child of the quote server span", client is not null && quote is not null && client.ParentSpanId == quote.SpanId, "");
Dojo.Check("the tax server span is a child of the client span (traceparent did its job)", tax is not null && client is not null && tax.ParentSpanId == client.SpanId, "");
Dojo.Check("all in one trace", quote is not null && tax is not null && client is not null && tax.TraceId == quote.TraceId && client.TraceId == quote.TraceId, "");

steps.prompt: A nightly job reads 500 messages from a queue and processes them in one batch. Each message came from a different web request. How should the batch span relate to them?
options: Start the batch span as a new root and add a **link** to each message's span context
Make the batch span a child of the first message's span
Make it a child of all 500 (one span, 500 parents)
Copy every message's trace id into an attribute
steps.explain: A span has one parent but any number of links. Links keep each request's trace short and connect it to the batch that processed it, which backends draw as a jump between traces. Making it the child of one message would hide the other 499 and stretch that trace over hours.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: instrumenting .NET
steps.body: What you reach for when wiring or debugging telemetry in a .NET service.

toolkit.what: The Aspire dashboard as a stand-alone local viewer: traces, metrics, structured logs from any OTLP app, no backend to set up.
flags: the UI (http://localhost:18888; the log prints a login link with a token)
its OTLP/gRPC endpoint on the port your app already uses (OTLP/HTTP is 18890)
skip the token, only on your own machine
toolkit.when: local development: see your spans before a Collector exists

toolkit.what: Where AddOtlpExporter() sends everything; with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL picks gRPC or HTTP.
flags: grpc (the .NET default, port 4317) or http/protobuf (4318, /v1/traces is appended)
toolkit.when: every deploy: the same build, different destinations

toolkit.what: Watch a running process's Meter instruments live, no SDK or exporter needed (they are the same System.Diagnostics.Metrics).
flags: meters to show; System.Runtime for GC, thread pool, exceptions
toolkit.when: checking a new instrument records before wiring dashboards

toolkit.what: Print every span, metric and log the SDK exports (package OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Console): the fastest "is anything produced at all?" check.
flags: the SDK's own self-diagnostics log, for export failures
toolkit.when: spans are missing and you do not know whether production or export is broken

steps.prompt: Match the symptom to the first tool to reach for.
pairs: No spans at all from the service: produced or not?
Want to see traces locally without a backend
Is my new Counter recording in the running process?
Same build must send to staging's Collector

steps.title: Carry the trace through a queue
prompt: `POST /orders/{id:int}` puts a message on an in-memory queue (a `Channel<Message>`), and a background `Worker` processes it later.
The trace stops at the queue. Finish the instrumentation (everything else is in the starter):
1. **Producer**, in the endpoint: a span **`orders publish`** of kind **Producer**, with `messaging.destination.name` = `orders`, and
2. **Consumer**, in `Worker`: **extract** the context from the headers and start **`orders process`** of kind **Consumer** with the
extracted context as its **parent**, with `messaging.destination.name` = `orders` and `app.order.id` = the id (an int).
starter: var msg = new Message(id, new Dictionary<string, string>());
record Message(int OrderId, Dictionary<string, string> Headers);
public static readonly ActivitySource Source = new("Orders.Api");
protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stop)
solution: var msg = new Message(id, new Dictionary<string, string>());
record Message(int OrderId, Dictionary<string, string> Headers);
public static readonly ActivitySource Source = new("Orders.Api");
protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stop)
using var process = Telemetry.Source.StartActivity("orders process", ActivityKind.Consumer, parent.ActivityContext);
hints: Producer: `using (var send = Telemetry.Source.StartActivity("orders publish", ActivityKind.Producer)) { ... Inject(new PropagationContext(send.Context, Baggage.Current), msg.Headers, (h, k, v) => h[k] = v); ... }`

Consumer: `var parent = Propagators.DefaultTextMapPropagator.Extract(default, msg.Headers, (h, k) => h.TryGetValue(k, out var v) ? [v] : []);` then `StartActivity("orders process", ActivityKind.Consumer, parent.ActivityContext)`.
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
DojoWeb.Status("POST /orders/41 is accepted", 202, await http.PostAsync("/orders/41", null));
var send = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.DisplayName == "orders publish");
var process = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.DisplayName == "orders process");
Dojo.Check("an orders publish span", send is not null, "Spans: " + string.Join(", ", DojoOtel.Spans.Select(a => a.DisplayName)));
Dojo.Eq("publish is a Producer span", "Producer", send?.Kind.ToString());
Dojo.Eq("publish names the destination", "orders", DojoOtel.Tag(send, "messaging.destination.name"));
var server = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.Kind == ActivityKind.Server);
Dojo.Check("publish is a child of the request", send is not null && server is not null && send.ParentSpanId == server.SpanId, "");
Dojo.Check("an orders process span", process is not null, "");
Dojo.Eq("process is a Consumer span", "Consumer", process?.Kind.ToString());
Dojo.Check("process continues the same trace", process is not null && send is not null && process.TraceId == send.TraceId, "different trace ids: the context did not travel with the message");
Dojo.Check("process is a child of publish", process is not null && send is not null && process.ParentSpanId == send.SpanId, "");
Dojo.Check("app.order.id is the int 41", process?.GetTagItem("app.order.id") is int dojoId && dojoId == 41, "");
DojoWeb.Status("a second order", 202, await http.PostAsync("/orders/42", null));
var second = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.DisplayName == "orders process" && Equals(a.GetTagItem("app.order.id"), 42));
Dojo.Check("each message keeps its own trace", second is not null && process is not null && second.TraceId != process.TraceId, "");
